subject: Post-call: model fit & tool-calling evals - next steps

Subject: Post-call: model fit & tool-calling evals - next steps

Hi Jenna - great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Summary of the call:
- Finata uses LLMs to extract structured invoice data (vendor, line items, tax, totals) and to populate accounting workflows.
- Key constraints: strict JSON schema for downstream systems, deterministic field typing for amounts/dates, and auditability for regressions when models update.
- Volume: ~3k-5k documents/day with spikes to 12k/monthly peak. Latency target: <350ms tail for single-document parse; batch throughput also important.

What we recommend next: 
1) Evaluation plan: Redwood will run a 2-week model-fit evaluation with your sample set and our structured-output tests (JSON schema compliance, field-level precision/recall).
2) Deliverables: prompt set we used, raw outputs, a summary PDF with per-field metrics, and a short demo of function-calling retry behavior for idempotent writes.
3) Technical lead call: schedule a 30-45m session with your eng team + Rishi to align on schema, retries, and logging.
4) Decision criteria: pass rates for schema validation (>98%), acceptable regression delta (<2% on key fields), and latency/cost targets.

Attachments: I attached an initial prompt set template and evaluation rubric. I will follow up with Rishi to share baseline models and the benchmark link.

Next steps (proposed):
- Rishi to send recommended model variants and test harness by EOD tomorrow.
- Jenna to share a representative sample (anonymized) and the exact JSON schema for invoice payload.
- Marissa to schedule the tech sync for next week.

Thanks - talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Thanks Marissa - this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We can provide an anonymized sample set (~2.5k docs) by EOD Monday.
- Our JSON schema is strict; we can't accept missing fields for tax or currency. I will attach the schema to the samples.
- Concern: previous vendor updates introduced regressions where the model sometimes changed field types (e.g., amount as string vs number). We need tests that catch those types of regressions automatically.
- On function/tool calling: we need guaranteed idempotency for downstream POSTs. If your retry logic replays a non-idempotent operation we could duplicate invoices. Can you outline how Redwood approaches retries and dedup?

Would appreciate Rishi's recommended models and the benchmark link you mentioned. Also, can you include an example of a failed vs. corrected output where the model fixed a schema violation?

Thanks,
Jenna Morris
Head of Platform Integrations | Finata, Inc.
jenna@finata.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Jenna Morris <jenna@finata.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-30T08:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit & tool-calling evals - next steps

Hi Jenna - Rishi here (solutions). Follow-up with concrete recommendations and how we test JSON schema compliance and function-calling retries.

Recommended models (start with these variants):
- redwood-open-7b-quant (recommended baseline for cost/latency) - good at structured output when paired with constrained decoding and schema enforcement.
- redwood-compat-13b-fp16 (higher accuracy, higher cost) - use for critical fields with strict precision (amounts, tax IDs).
- fallback: redwood-llm-small (fast, cheap) for best-effort enrichment when primary model is overloaded.

Benchmark link: https://benchmarks.redwood.ai/finata-invoice-parse (contains baseline metrics on your publicish dataset + our synthetic edge cases).

How we validate JSON schema compliance:
- We run a multi-stage pipeline: (1) generation with constrained prompts and structured-output guidance, (2) automatic JSON parse + schema validation (we use your provided JSON Schema), (3) a repair pass where the model is prompted to return a corrected JSON if the first pass fails, (4) if still invalid after N retries (configurable, default 2), we mark as failure and surface to human review.
- We include field-level validators for dates/amounts and type coercion rules (e.g., coerce numeric-looking strings to numbers only if within tolerance).
- All attempts are logged with token counts and model variant used for auditing.

Retries & idempotency:
- For function/tool calling we recommend using an idempotency key (we'll provide an SDK helper). Retries are performed client-side with exponential backoff; Redwood's function-calling wrapper can attach an idempotency key and dedup by key on downstream writes.
- For non-idempotent downstream APIs you can opt for a dry-run write to our gateway which returns the intended effect without committing, or we can route calls through a Job queue that performs single-commit semantics.

Attached are: finata_prompt_set.csv (sample prompts + expected JSON), raw_tool_evals.json (raw outputs from baseline models), and eval_summary_finata.pdf (human-reviewed summary).

Suggested evaluation metrics (we'll produce these):
- JSON schema pass rate (target >98%)
- Field-level precision/recall (amounts, vendor, invoice_number)
- Type-stability metric (how often field types change across model upgrades)
- Latency P95 and cost per document

If that looks good I can kick off the baseline run with the sample set as soon as you share it. Propose a tech sync on Wednesday 2026-07-07 10:00 PT.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com
